title: Root-Zone, IPM, Propagation and Canopy Troubleshooting Stations

content.overview: These stations require Technician II to combine process execution with troubleshooting discipline. Fertigation and irrigation evidence must retain recipe identity, measurement verification and crop/media context; IPM, propagation and canopy evidence must preserve sampling quality, sanitation, cultivar or stage context and treatment-authority boundaries.

vocabulary.definition: A recommendation limited to the verified crop, media, process, authorization and evidence conditions supplied by the case.
The separation between interpreting plant-health evidence and having legal or facility authorization to select, mix or apply a regulated treatment.
Comparison of outcome evidence against defined process, batch, cultivar or stage context without assuming a cause that the evidence does not establish.

sections.title: Execute the approved batch before troubleshooting it
sections.body: Verify material identity, approved recipe, sequence, measurement readiness and actual results. An abnormal pH, EC or root-zone value requires the verification steps defined by the process before major correction.

sections.title: Dryback and root-zone trends are contextual
sections.body: Trend meaning depends on crop stage, media, irrigation history, distribution and plant demand. The lab prohibits universal dryback assumptions detached from those variables.

sections.title: IPM outcome evidence is multi-round evidence
sections.body: Comparable sampling effort, mapped scope, incidence, severity, trap evidence and intervention timing are evaluated together. A single favorable observation does not override a contradictory trend.

sections.title: Propagation and canopy performance need comparison groups
sections.body: Donor, batch, cultivar, stage, sanitation and environmental history help bound a performance problem. Technician II may identify the next verification step without claiming contamination, genotype effect or treatment need without support.

workedExamples: A fertigation value is out of expected range; verify meter readiness and sample identity before altering the approved recipe.
A propagation batch roots poorly while another batch under the same room conditions performs normally; compare donor, handling, sanitation and batch records before assigning an environmental cause.
commonMistakes: Changing an approved recipe without authority.
Using one root-zone target across all media and stages.
Declaring IPM success from an isolated low count.
Claiming genetics or contamination without comparative evidence.
content.practicalApplication: Rotate through Practical C, D and E preparation cases and produce one bounded troubleshooting memo per station with verified facts, uncertainty, next check and escalation boundary.
content.summary: Advanced production troubleshooting preserves process identity, comparable evidence and authority boundaries across root-zone, IPM, propagation and canopy work.

primaryVisuals.title: Integrated fertigation and root-zone station
primaryVisuals.alt: Station workflow verifying approved recipe and material identity, measuring-system readiness, irrigation delivery, root-zone trend and crop context before a bounded troubleshooting recommendation, with unauthorized recipe redesign or major chemistry decisions routed to escalation.
primaryVisuals.caption: Verify batch identity, measurement quality, delivery and crop context before troubleshooting the root zone. Do not convert diagnostic skill into independent recipe-design authority.

primaryVisuals.title: Integrated IPM propagation and canopy evidence
primaryVisuals.alt: Integrated plant-health and performance workflow combining comparable multi-round IPM sampling, biosecurity controls, donor or batch evidence, canopy and flowering context, and uncertainty while keeping regulated treatment decisions and unsupported contamination or genotype claims outside Technician II authority.
primaryVisuals.caption: Combine multi-round IPM evidence with donor, sanitation, stage and mapped canopy response. Preserve biosecurity and do not overstate contamination, genotype causation or treatment authority.
